description_full: Scorpio Tankers Inc., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the seaborne transportation of crude oil and refined petroleum products worldwide. As of March 19, 2026, its fleet consisted of 90 wholly owned tankers, including 34 LR2, 42MR, and 14 Handymax. Scorpio Tankers Inc. was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Monaco.
ceo_bio: Mr. Emanuele A. Lauro | Founder, Chairman & CEO | Age 47
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 24 people. Revenue per employee of $39.1M ranks in the top quartile among Energy peers, improving at 8%/yr — growing workforce leverage.
financial_summary: Scorpio Tankers Inc. is a mid-cap energy business with a $4.1B market cap on $938M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -16% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +5.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 8% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.
The company is burning through $81M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 4.4×.

Shareholder yield of 2.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 16% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 39% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 16% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 38% and a beta of 0.64, it is more defensive than the market.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $61.24 (margin of safety -32%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 27%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $49.97 to $77.19 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Energy peers: P/E 4.2 vs 13.4 and EV/EBITDA 3.1 vs 6.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 175% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of -2.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 15.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $108 on average, 33% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 19% clears the cost of capital of 8.2% by 11pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.15).
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.43x.
ROE of 11% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.2x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 13pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $151.9M.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -15.6% over 3 years and 0.5% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 67%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 19.1% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 10.2% on average.
Analysts expect -40.9% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 15.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 74%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (10 sales, net $19.0B sold).
It returns 2.0% a year to shareholders (0.0% in buybacks and 3.7% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years, raising it 28.8% a year over the last five.
people: With about 24 employees, each generates about $39.1M of revenue, 19.3x the Energy median, and productivity has risen 7.8% a year.

The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
